svg.title: AIC⚡DC Intended Architecture — second engine and web pull
svg.desc: The intended architecture after adding Google Antigravity as a second agent backend beside Claude Code, and a Web Pull feature. One Python process exposes jrpc-oo over WebSocket to a Lit browser client. An engine router mounts both adapters under one RPC namespace and publishes a capability descriptor so surfaces with no counterpart are hidden rather than stubbed. Exactly one engine is master per session; the other is reachable as a one-shot consultant. The Claude adapter owns an external claude CLI subprocess authenticated by OAuth; the Antigravity adapter owns a bundled localharness subprocess authenticated by a Gemini API key. The agy CLI is shown rejected. Web Pull lands fetched content in the working tree, which re-indexes.
svg.text: Second agent backend (Google Antigravity) beside Claude Code · Web Pull · one RPC namespace · capability descriptor
Pink outline and NEW badge mark what this plan adds. Everything else exists today. Decision IDs refer to specs5/plan-ag/decisions.md.
One set of call sites. Per-engine differences resolved through the capability descriptor, never through an engine-name branch (AG-R-4).
Features consume the router, not an engine. Anything landing bytes in the working tree triggers incremental re-index.
Exactly one engine is master per session (AG-1). The other is reachable as a one-shot consultant (AG-7).
Engine Router — one RPC namespace + capability descriptor (AG-3, AG-9)
Both adapters mount under the same namespace, so the browser's 43 call sites across 59 files do not fork. The descriptor declares which
surfaces each engine can feed; a surface with no counterpart is hidden rather than filled with a synthesised value.
chat · cancel · resume · fork · model · budget
SDK taxonomy to server-push events · drains to ResultMessage
chat · cancel · resume by conversation_id · multi-model
Step to Event · flat, trajectory_id + depth · tokens only
External processes — owned by an SDK, not by AIC⚡DC
Each keeps its own context window, prompt cache, compaction and credentials. The two credential paths are separate and separately billed (AG-R-8).

to Gemini API · protobuf over local WebSocket
auth: API key or Vertex — no OAuth path at 0.1.15
browser suite the SDK does not expose.

permission, and its stream omits file content,
so no diff can be rendered. Not drawn as a
dependency because nothing depends on it.
Reaches Antigravity as plain Python callables, not through MCP (AG-4) — simpler here than the in-process MCP bridge the Claude adapter needs.
Unchanged by this plan. One repo root, one working tree, one master writing to it (AG-10).

The two engines never share a credential, a context window, or a working-tree write. Concurrent masters on one tree is explicitly out of scope (AG-R-7). Verified 2026-08-30 against google-antigravity 0.1.15 and agy 1.1.22.
